idiom_name: per-table ActiveRecord models with an abstract base class or concern; delegated_type for mixed reads
implementation_notes: ActiveRecord already gives one table per model, so this mapping needs no configuration: declare each concrete class as its own model over its own table, keep the shared columns in an abstract base class (self.abstract_class = true) or an ActiveSupport::Concern, and inherit only for Ruby-level behaviour. Rails' native inheritance answer is single table inheritance via a type column, and Rails 6.1+ ships delegated_type for the mixed-read problem - the API documentation describes this mapping's weakness precisely ('all concrete subclasses must persist all the shared attributes themselves in their own tables ... you can't pull from both tables at once and use a consistent OFFSET/LIMIT scheme'). Choose the per-table route when tables must stay leaf-local; choose STI or delegated types when hierarchy-wide queries and pagination matter.
pitfalls: A subclass of a non-abstract ActiveRecord model with a type column silently switches to single table inheritance, so rows come back as the wrong class.
Per-table primary keys are independent sequences: an id is only meaningful together with its table, so cross-hierarchy references need a UUID or a delegating table.
Renaming a shared column means editing every model and every migration; there is no schema-level link between engineers.name and managers.name.
